title: Bigger Pieces Have Bills

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Fan mail. Addressed to The Very Impressive Army.
directions: [board: a teller window. Pip is at the counter holding up a small envelope addressed to The Very Impressive Army.]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: It is a bill. Three crystals, due when your turn starts.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: My fan is very picky about timing.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Hello. We bought that Hi on C three. Does it owe anything?
directions: [board: C three, with the Hi we bought last time standing on it.]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Nothing. Tier one never gets mail.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Upkeep is the toll a big piece pays, at your own turn start.
directions: [card: TIER MEANS HOW FAR A PIECE HAS CLIMBED · the Hi is tier one · the Hono is tier two · the Tanka is tier three]
[board: one coin drops through a small gate in the counter as the word lands.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Tier one owes nothing. Tier two owes one. Tier three owes two.
directions: [board: three envelopes stamped 0, 1 and 2, in front of the Hi, the Hono and the Tanka. The bank counter shows two.]

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Then we let the Hi go. Off the board, and we save a fortune.
directions: [card: KEEPING A PIECE MEANS PAYING ITS ENVELOPE · nobody pays, that piece walks away]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Letting the Hi go saves zero crystals. And tier one may never be let go.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: My loophole has become a regular hole.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Extremely responsible is doing a lot of work in that plan.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Nothing, one, two.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: And tier one always stays.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Bank: two.
directions: [card: ALL THREE] [card: THE HI AND THE TANKA]
[board: two crystals in the bank. The envelope on the Hi lies open. The other two are sealed. Nothing moves.]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: All three envelopes: three.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: The Hi and the Tanka: two.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Which card can two crystals pay for?

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Put a finger on one, or take your time and look at both.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Two crystals cannot open all three. So the Hono is let go.
directions: [sfx: bill thud] [board: the second card lights. The Hono steps back from the counter and off the table, its envelope still sealed. Then both crystals slide onto the Tanka envelope and it opens.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Then two crystals opened the Tanka envelope, and the Hi owed nothing.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: We do not pay part of it. We keep less of us.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Proves what two crystals pay. Not which pieces we want.
directions: [card: EVIDENCE · proves: two crystals keep the Hi and the Tanka · also payable: the Hi and the Hono, or the Hi alone · not checked: which pieces this army actually wants]

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: I will pay this turn's bill from this turn's payday. Here is a receipt.
directions: [card: pay the bill from today's payday]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Your receipt cannot mine.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: This turn's bill comes before healing and payday. Today's income can pay next turn's bill.
directions: [board: Pip lowers the receipt onto a crystal square. It does not dig. Then it goes into the drawer marked PIP'S AMENDMENTS (PENDING).]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: The Standing Bill comes back every turn you own a Hono or a Tanka.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: One game for your table. Put counters beside each card, then add them up.
directions: [card: TABLE GAME · counters beside each card · add them up · move that many crystals out of the bank first]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Nothing, one, two.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: If your bank covers every bill, payment is automatic. Otherwise, choose an affordable group to keep. All tier one pieces must stay. The review upkeep setting also lets you release bigger pieces voluntarily. Losing your last piece loses the game.

supplement.title: Pay before healing and Place
supplement.body:
Enough crystals: payment is automatic.
Otherwise choose an affordable group. All T1 must stay.
Review upkeep each turn: optionally release T2 or T3.
No pieces left means elimination.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: A newly promoted piece pays its new tier bill on your next turn, not again today. A home occupation win is checked before any of these bills.

supplement.title: Tomorrow’s tier bill
supplement.body:
Promotion now → new upkeep next own turn.
Home win check → upkeep → full heal → Place.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: And tier one always stays.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Stopping here is fine. Next time we count somebody else's trip.

question: Which card can two crystals pay for?
